english.title: Wear uniform / dress having appearance of uniform / dress bearing regimental mark of HM Forces without permission
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a person not serving in HM military forces, wore, without His Majesty’s permission,

(A)_[a uniform]_
(B)_[dress having the appearance of a uniform]_
(C)_[dress bearing the regimental or other distinctive mark]_

of the military force, namely **(..SPECIFY MILITARY FORCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 2 of the Uniforms Act 1894.

english.notes:
(i) See section 2 of the Uniforms Act 1894 for the defence for stage plays etc.
(ii) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.
